messages:
sophia: Heads-up — customer onboarding hit an SSL issue with our py async client behind a corporate proxy. Works with sync client but async fails with cert verify.
leo: What error do they see?
sophia: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: self signed certificate in certificate chain` from inside uvloop.
sophia: Env: REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://private.redwood.internal, HTTPS_PROXY=http://10.10.0.2:8080, SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/private/org-ca.pem. Using redwood.AsyncClient() with no extra args.
amir: Quick check — does curl with --cacert /etc/ssl/private/org-ca.pem + --proxy succeed?
sophia: Yes curl works. Sync client (requests) also works when I export SSL_CERT_FILE. Only async fails.
leo: So likely aiohttp connector not loading SSL_CERT_FILE when proxy settings are present — I've seen this before. We construct an SSLContext in the transport and forget to call load_verify_locations(cafile=...) when proxy is set.
amir: Repro locally with minimal script to confirm. I wrote this: ```python
import ssl, asyncio, aiohttp
ssl_ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/private/org-ca.pem')
async def main():
    conn = aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ssl_ctx)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=conn) as s:
        async with s.get('https://private.redwood.internal', proxy='http://10.10.0.2:8080') as r:
            print(await r.text()[:100])
asyncio.run(main())
```
leo: Running that works for me too. So workaround is to accept ssl argument on AsyncClient or to set up a custom transport that honors SSL_CERT_FILE.
sophia: Customer can't modify their app easily. Any chance we can make SDK honor SSL_CERT_FILE automatically for async clients when present in env? That would match requests behavior.
amir: Agreed. Action: (1) patch AsyncTransport to check env SSL_CERT_FILE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and pass cafile into ssl.create_default_context OR call load_verify_locations on the context it already uses; (2) add CI test with proxy+custom CA using localproxy container; (3) add docs blurb in Dedicated onboarding under networking + custom CA.
leo: I'll open a PR and add a small unit test that spins up a proxy stub and uses certs from fixtures. Low risk.
sophia: Also noticed confusing precedence at work: REDWOOD_BASE_URL vs passing base_url= in code vs REDWOOD_HOSTNAME env used by infra scripts. Customer had REDWOOD_HOSTNAME set and our client was constructing base_url by joining scheme+REDWOOD_HOSTNAME which ignored REDWOOD_BASE_URL. We should document the precedence clearly.
amir: Yes — add a note in SDK config page: param > REDWOOD_BASE_URL env > REDWOOD_HOSTNAME legacy var. Also log a warning when multiple overlapping env vars exist.
docs-bot: Created docs issue #876: "py-sdk: document env var precedence for base_url and custom CA guidance for async client".
sophia: Thanks. For support replies: ask customers to verify with curl --proxy and provide the CACERT path; suggest immediate workaround: instantiate AsyncClient with explicit ssl context: ```python
import ssl
from redwood import AsyncClient
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile='/etc/ssl/private/org-ca.pem')
client = AsyncClient(base_url='https://private.redwood.internal', http_proxy='http://10.10.0.2:8080', ssl=ctx)
```
leo: I'll link this thread in the issue and assign the PR to Amir. Good catch.
